To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

abnormal liver enzyme levels late after stem cell transplantation (SCT) are more prevalent in children who were older at SCT and who were transplanted for a benign disease, but are less prevalent than reported in previous reports.

the prevalence of elevated AST and ALT levels 2 years after allogeneic HSCT is lower than previously reported, and that older age at HSCT (≥5 years) and a diagnosis of a benign haematological disorder are risk factors for elevated liver enzymes 2years after HSCT.

elevated AST and ALT levels were found in 25% of children 2 years after transplantation and that older age at transplantation and a benign disease were the most important risk factors for elevated liver enzyme values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevalence of abnormal serum aminotransferase levels at 2 years post-transplant in a Dutch HSCT centre and the risk factors for these abnormal liver enzyme levels.
the prevalence of elevated AST and ALT at 2 years post HSCT in children transplated at our Dutch centre.
the study of the prevalence of elevated AST and ALT values in children 2 years after a haematopoietetic stem cell transplantation (HCT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the risk of liver dysfunction after allogenic stem cell transplantation (SCT) depends on the conditioning regimen, donor type and the underlying disease, but also on the time of assessment of liver function and the type of laboratory test used.
elevated liver enzymes are common after HSCT but are not necessarily associated with liver disease.
the liver enzymes should be measured at 2 years and 5 years after HSCT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of abnormal LFTs late after HSCT is lower in children transplated in our centre than reported previously.
the prevalence of abnormal AST and ALT values late after HSCT is lower in children than in adults.
the prevalence of elevated AST and ALT values in children transplated at our centre at 2 years post-transplant was low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
abnormal liver enzyme values at 2years after HSCT are common and may precede clinical liver dysfunction.
elevated liver enzymes late after transplantation are not uncommon and that the underlying cause may differ depending on the patient's age at transplantation and diagnosis.
elevated liver enzymes are not uncommon late after HSCT, especially in children who were older at HSCT.
